A federal judge has asked to be informed about the details of any agreement that may have led a company owned by Elon Musk to withdraw its antitrust allegations against Apple. Here are the relevant details.

Judge seeks to see any deal reached with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a motion in court seeking to voluntarily dismiss (without prejudice) the portion of their lawsuit against Apple and OpenAI that was filed last year concerning Apple.

According to the original lawsuit filings, Apple and OpenAI were accused of conspiring to prevent other competing AI apps from gaining exposure on the App Store through a deal integrating ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence. Both Apple and OpenAI have denied the allegations.

In filings submitted earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI only stated that they had "reached a settlement of the claims against Apple in this case," and emphasised that they were not seeking to withdraw the claims against OpenAI.

According to POLITICO, which first reported the story, Judge Mark Pittman, who is presiding over the case, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit to the court "any agreement or series of agreements related to the settlement of plaintiffs' claims against Apple in this case."

The order was issued in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI, which sought to compel X and SpaceXAI to surrender their settlement agreement with Apple. Pittman also ordered the relevant companies to respond to OpenAI's motion by noon on 17 September.
